Alex: Ran an nsys trace on nightly perf for the 2.7B config — noticing a recurring stall during decode when fused-flash-attn and KV cache are both active. perf timeline shows long GPU idle gaps aligned with KV write bursts. attaching quick notes.
Maria: can you paste the nsys command you ran? also which commit/sha triggered this?
Alex: ran on commit 0c4f3a2 — repros locally. command:
```
nsys profile --output=run_190824 --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=kernel --backtrace=yes --sample=none --force-overwrite yes --target-processes=all -- python -m perf.runner --model 2.7B --batch 2 --seq 2048
```
Jin: saw something similar last week. perfetto view showed dense vertical stripes (KV activity) right after each attn kernel, and the SM efficiency drops to ~32% during those windows. nvprof counters look like mem_dep stalls spike.
Sam: do we have a flamegraph snippet? are the stripes host->device memcpy or kernel writes? could be prefetch touching KV pages on write path.
Alex: perfetto screenshot: blue = memcpy H2D, orange = kernel. The pattern is: attn kernel -> tiny H2D -> kv_write_kernel -> 40ms gap -> attn kernel. The gap correlates with host-side serialization in the KV writer thread (we see GPU queues idle).
Luke: that sounds like writeback serialization. We did enable prefetching for KV pages in the last heuristic change (PR #3146) — maybe it's too aggressive and triggers synchronous writebacks.
Maria: @Luke which heuristic exactly? the one that prefetches next N slots when occupancy < threshold?
Luke: yes — code is in runtime/kv/prefetcher.cc. default prefetch depth = 4, and we added forced writeback on collision to avoid stale reads. If prefetcher and writeback race, writes get serialized on a single stream.
Sam: can we try disabling prefetcher and re-run nsys? also try running with async_writeback=true so writes don't block the default compute stream.
Alex: already did quick runs: baseline (prefetch=4, async_writeback=false) p50 decode = 102ms. pref=0 gives p50 95ms. pref=4 + async_writeback=true gives p50 94ms. so looks like prefetch+sync_writeback is the culprit.
Jin: what about KV size/tiling? on long sequences we touch more shards and prefetch expands the working set — maybe causing L2 thrash and longer writeback times.
Alex: nvprof counters:
```
warp_serialize: 1.8e6
stall_mem_dep: +48%
l2_throughput: up 1.4x
sm_efficiency: down 18%
```
Maria: interesting. if L2 traffic increases, attn kernels pay for it. I think two mitigations: (1) make prefetch heuristic workload-aware (don't prefetch when seq_len>1024), (2) make writeback use separate CUDA stream + host pinned buffer to avoid blocking default stream.
Luke: agree. quick patch idea: runtime/kv/prefetcher.cc add `if (seq_len > 1024 || batch>4) prefetch_depth=0;` and change writer to use `cudaMemcpyAsync` onto pinned host staging and dispatch writes on a dedicated stream.
Sam: can you try a run with prefetch disabled on a whale trace (seq2048) and attach nsys timeline? that will give a clean compare.
Alex: will run 3 configs and post traces: (A) master, (B) pref=0, (C) master+async_wb_stream. ETA ~30m.
perfbot: perf-bot: nightly/regressions: decode p50 for model-2.7B increased by 6.2% on commit 0c4f3a2 vs baseline. linked: https://perf.redwood.local/compare/0c4f3a2
Maria: ok let's not roll this out. @eng-runtime can we add a short-term kill-switch env var (KV_PREFETCH=0) to toggle in prod if needed?
Luke: yep will add KV_PREFETCH env + runtime flag by EOD.
Jin: once Alex posts traces I can do a deeper nvprof scalars pass and try to attribute stalls to specific memory ops.
Alex: uploaded traces to /tmp/nsys/190824_{A,B,C}.nsys and perfetto links. I'll follow up with perf screenshots. thanks all :thumbsup:
